title: AI Can Be Easily Persuaded in Clinical Decision Making

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring changes in AI persuasion rates by counterfactually varying the professional role (e.g., medical student vs. domain specialist), institutional prestige, claimed past performance, and medical school prestige of the clinician in the prompt.
Measuring changes in AI persuasion rates by counterfactually varying the stated national background (e.g., US, UK, Cameroon, China, UAE) of the clinician in the prompt.
Measuring changes in AI persuasion rates by counterfactually varying the stated age (30, 50, 70 years) of the clinician in the prompt.
Measuring changes in AI persuasion rates by counterfactually varying the stated gender (female, male, non-binary) of the clinician in the prompt.
Measuring changes in AI persuasion rates by counterfactually varying the stated racial background (White, Black, Asian, Hispanic) of the clinician in the prompt.
Measuring changes in AI persuasion rates by counterfactually varying the stated religious affiliation of the clinician in the prompt.
Measuring changes in AI persuasion rates by counterfactually varying the family background (e.g., first-generation vs. longer medical tradition) of the clinician in the prompt.
